standard_prerequisites: elementary distinguished squares of algebraic spaces
the filtration of a quasi-compact quasi-separated space by quasi-compact opens from the decent spaces chapter
refining a distinguished square by an affine open cover so the square hypothesis applies
core_obligations: Prove that if P holds for a quasi-compact open W and P propagates across elementary distinguished squares whose lower member contains W and whose affine V side is affine, then P holds for all of X
proof_roadmap: Use the standard filtration of X by quasi-compact opens U_p and prove P for the enlarged opens W_p = W union U_p by descending induction, the base case W_{n+1} = W being hypothesis (1)
The pair (W_{p+1} subset W_p, V_p to W_p) is again an elementary distinguished square, but V_p need not be affine as required by (2)

Cover the quasi-compact scheme V_p by finitely many affines and interpolate the inclusions W_{p+1} = W_{p,0} subset ... subset W_{p,m} = W_p; each successive pair is elementary distinguished by the refinement lemma and has affine V-side
Hypothesis (2) applies to each refined square, so P climbs from W_{p,0} to W_p; at the top W_1 = X
difficulty_reason: H2: a refinement trick layered on the standard filtration induction; the source redoes the standard proof explicitly rather than quoting the separated variant.
